parts: dy/dx is the rate of change of y with respect to x. For a circle, dA/dr = 2πr (8π when r = 4).
Differentials: f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f'(x)Δx. For √26: f(x) = √x, x = 25, Δx = 1, so √26 ≈ 5 + 1/(2·5) = 5.1.

The slope of the tangent at (x₁, y₁) is dy/dx there; the tangent is y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). The normal has slope −1/m (−dx/dy). A tangent is parallel to the x-axis where dy/dx = 0, and parallel to the y-axis where dx/dy = 0. Curves cut at right angles when the product of their slopes at the point of intersection is −1.
Rolle: if f is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b) and f(a) = f(b), there is c in (a, b) with f'(c) = 0. (f(x) = x on [−1, 1] fails, since f(−1) ≠ f(1).)
Lagrange's MVT: if f is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), there is c with f'(c) = [f(b) − f(a)]/(b − a).
f is increasing where f'(x) > 0 and decreasing where f'(x) < 0. Find the critical points (f' = 0) and test the sign of f' in each interval.

At a critical point c: f''(c) < 0 gives a local maximum and f''(c) > 0 a local minimum (second derivative test). For word problems, write the quantity as a function of one variable, differentiate, set to zero and check with f''.
In cost problems: AC = C/x, MC = dC/dx; AC is minimum where AC = MC.
